title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Careers, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This page collects the canonical company handbook content for 'Working at Redwood': role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, hiring and new-hire onboarding flow, and the core internal tools guide. It is intended for new hires, managers, and cross-functional partners who need a single reference for policies and practical procedures.

Section 1 — Working at Redwood (Intro & Principles)

Short intro
- Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production LLM inference; our culture values ownership, operational excellence, and customer empathy.
- We expect clear communication, asynchronous documentation, and measurable outcomes.

Core principles
1. Ship reliable, observable systems: prioritize production quality and SLO-driven work.
2. Be customer-obsessed: understand downstream use cases and cost/latency tradeoffs.
3. Learn fast: measure, iterate, and share learnings across teams.

Section 2 — Roles & Career Ladders

Scope
- This section summarizes role families, typical responsibilities, and career ladder progression. Detailed individual ladders (levels, competencies, promotion criteria) are maintained by People Ops and Engineering Managers; reference links are provided in Related Pages.

Role families (high level)
- Engineering: Serving Runtime, Platform, Infra, SRE, Developer Experience, Private Deployments.
- Product & Design: Product Managers, UX/UI Designers, Product Ops.
- Research & Applied ML: Model onboarding, quantization, evals, inference research.
- Go-to-market: Sales, Solutions, Customer Success, Growth.
- People Ops & Finance: Recruiting, HRBP, Payroll, Legal & Compliance.

Career ladder summary (one-line expectations by level)
- IC-1 / New Grad: Executes well on discrete tasks, seeks mentorship.
- IC-2 / Mid: Owns well-scoped projects, contributes to design reviews, reliable delivery.
- IC-3 / Senior: Owns cross-team features, mentors others, influences architecture.
- IC-4 / Staff: Leads complex, cross-functional initiatives, defines technical strategy.
- IC-5 / Principal: Shapes org-level direction, represents Redwood externally for technical topics.

Manager career path
- Manager-1: Manages small teams, hires ICs, runs performance cycles.
- Manager-2: Manages managers or larger organizations, drives cross-team prioritization.

Promotion & calibration process (numbered steps)
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet: impact summary, examples, 3-5 artifacts (PRs, design docs, metrics).
2. Manager completes eval form and collects peer feedback.
3. Calibration committee reviews packet; committee includes manager, EM peers, and People Ops rep.
4. Decision and compensation update communicated; candidate gets written feedback and next steps.

Section 3 — Benefits & Perks (Executive Summary)

Benefits table (summary)
| Category | What we provide | Ownership / Contacts | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health & Wellness | Medical (PPO/HMO), dental, vision | People Ops benefits team | Coverage begins first day of month after hire; see benefits portal for plans. |
| Paid Time Off | 20 days PTO (accrual), 12 weeks parental leave | People Ops | PTO encourages recharge; manager must approve >5 contiguous days. |
| Compensation | Competitive base + equity, annual salary review | Finance & People Ops | Compensation bands maintained by People Ops; salary review cadence is annual. |
| Professional Development | $2,000 yearly learning stipend | People Ops | Submit receipts via expense system; manager approval recommended. |
| Commuter / Remote | Stipend for home office, flexible remote policy | People Ops | See Remote Handbook for region-specific guidance. |
| Wellness perks | Mental health EAP, gym stipend, quarterly wellness events | People Ops | Confidential through EAP vendor. |

How to access benefits
- Benefits portal (link in People Ops Confluence) contains plan details, enrollment deadlines, and vendor contacts.
- For urgent coverage questions, contact benefits@redwood-inference.com.

Section 4 — Hiring (Overview & Best Practices)

Hiring philosophy
- Hire for ownership and technical curiosity. We prioritize bias-mitigated processes and diverse candidate slates. Interview panels should reflect role seniority and cross-functional perspectives.

Standard interview stages
1. Recruiter screen (role match, compensation expectations, logistics).
2. Hiring manager screen (skills fit, team fit).
3. Technical assessment or take-home (if applicable).
4. Onsite / loop: 4-6 interviews including system design, coding/problem solving, product/behavioral, bar-raiser.
5. Debrief & hire/no-hire decision.

Interviewer guidelines (bullet list)
- Use the rubric: behavioral, technical, and ownership dimensions.
- Rate against level guide, not against other candidates.
- Provide specific examples in feedback; do not use subjective labels.
- Avoid questions outside the job's scope; follow accommodation requests.

Offer & onboarding timeline (table)
| Stage | Target SLAs |
|---|---|
| Offer creation | Recruiter + Hiring Manager: 3 business days after approval |
| Offer acceptance | Candidate: target 7 calendar days |
| Preboarding tasks completed | Candidate: 5 business days before start |
| New hire first day | Orientation and team onboarding scheduled |

Inclusive hiring & accommodations
- Provide accommodations for interviews; contact recruiting@redwood-inference.com.
- Ensure interview panels are balanced and trained on unconscious bias.

Section 5 — New-hire Onboarding (Checklist & 30/60/90)

Before day 1 (preboarding)
- Send welcome packet with links: company handbook, security training, calendar invites for orientation.
- Provision accounts: email, Slack, VPN, internal GitHub, payroll. Owners: People Ops & IT.

Day 1-7 (orientation)
- Day 1: People Ops orientation (policies, benefits), team intro, assigned buddy.
- Complete mandatory trainings: security, code of conduct, privacy, and role-specific compliance.

30/60/90 plan (manager & hire)
- 30 days: produce 1-2 small deliverables, meet key partners, complete ramp doc.
- 60 days: take ownership of a feature or service, present first findings to team.
- 90 days: lead a project end-to-end, contribute to roadmap planning.

Onboarding checklist (numbered)
1. Complete compliance & security training.
2. Join team channels and read team runbooks.
3. Set up local dev environment and run smoke tests.
4. Shadow on-call and review runbooks (if role applies).
5. Meet with manager for expectations and 30/60/90 goals.

Section 6 — Internal Tools Guide (Core tools, owners, quick links)

Purpose
- This section lists the primary internal tools new employees and managers need to use regularly, the SRE/Tooling owners, and a short how-to for common tasks. Keep this page as the lightweight index; deep links point to team-run docs for each tool.

Key tools (bulleted with owner and quick actions)
- Slack (All teams) — Owner: Engineering Productivity. Quick actions: join #team-* channels, enable 2FA, pin important messages.
- GitHub (code + PR process) — Owner: Eng Dev Tools. Quick actions: follow repo CODEOWNERS, use draft PRs, label bugs with 'regressions'.
- CI/CD (Argo/Tekton pipeline) — Owner: Eng Infra. Quick actions: rerun failed jobs, open infra-ops ticket for persistent failures.
- Service Catalog & Ownership (internal app) — Owner: Eng Platform. Quick actions: verify service contact, claim ownership for new services.
- Incident & Pager (PagerDuty / Opsgenie) — Owner: Eng SRE. Quick actions: acknowledge, follow incident runbook, run RCA template.
- Observability (Grafana/Lightstep/Prometheus) — Owner: Observability Team. Quick actions: run latency & error dashboards, create alerts per SLO.
- Expense & Benefits Portal (Concur/Workday) — Owner: Finance & People Ops. Quick actions: submit receipts, enroll in benefits.
- On-call rota & runbooks (Confluence runbooks) — Owner: Team SREs. Quick actions: review runbook, run post-incident checklist.

How-to snippets (examples)
- Requesting access (short procedure):
  1. Open an access request in the IT portal and tag the owning team.
  2. Your manager approves; IT provisions within 2 business days.
  3. Verify access and notify manager.

- Submitting a service ownership change (CLI example):
  1. Open an issue in the Service Catalog repo with new owner details.
  2. Reference the service ID and include migration plan.

Section 7 — Manager Responsibilities & Tools

Manager checklist (quarterly cycles)
- Run performance calibration with People Ops.
- Maintain clear role expectations and promotion conversations.
- Ensure psychological safety: regular 1:1s and team retros.
- Monitor on-call load and adjust rotations.

Manager tools (must-use)
- People Ops portal: headcount & comp planning.
- Performance system: write and share feedback notes.
- Recruiting dashboard: track pipeline and interview scorecards.

Section 8 — Policies & Exceptions

Key policy links (refer to full policies in Policies & Process)
- Remote & flexible work policy.
- Code of Conduct & anti-harassment policy.
- Security & acceptable use policy (mandatory).

Exceptions
- Requests for policy exceptions (e.g., remote work outside covered regions, non-standard benefits) are reviewed by People Ops + Legal. Submit requests via people-ops exceptions form; include justification and duration.

Section 9 — FAQs & Contacts

Common questions
- Who do I ask for sticker or hardware requests? — IT helpdesk (it@redwood-inference.com).
- Where are runbooks for critical services? — Team Confluence pages under eng-*-runbooks.
- How do I update a career ladder or raise a promotion question? — Talk to your manager and People Ops.

Important contacts
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood-inference.com
- Benefits team: benefits@redwood-inference.com
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood-inference.com
- IT / Access requests: it@redwood-inference.com
- Security (incident): security@redwood-inference.com

Maintenance & ownership
- Owner: People Ops (document owner).
- Review cadence: quarterly; reviewers: Eng Managers, Head of People Ops, Legal as needed.

Related pages
- See the linked career ladder pages, detailed benefits plan, and team-specific onboarding runbooks in the People Ops and Engineering space.
